newsitem.title: USA: New World Coffee plans to double stores.
newsitem.headline: New World Coffee plans to double stores.

text.p: New World Coffee Inc said Friday it expects to achieve significant net income profitability, to double the number of its stores and be in two new markets by year-end 1997.

The company said it told the Regional Investment Bankers Association in Houston that its goal for 1997 is to add at least 40 new stores, and that two leases have been signed already and twenty-six letters of intent issued.
The company said it also plans to enter the Boston and Washington D.C. markets during 1997.
The company said it expects to see "dramatic financial improvements in the third and fourth quarters of 1996" from recent expansion.
Since its initial public offering in the first quarter of 1996, New World has added six stores and recently announced the pending acquisition of the six-store Willoughby's chain.
In late morning trading the stock was off 1/16 after closing at 2 3/16.
